summary: This Docker Compose configuration defines a service called my_second_container that builds from the current directory, connects to an existing external network called my_network, and adds a custom hostname-to-IP mapping so the container can reach my_site.local at address 172.20.0.1.

explanations.8: extra_hosts lets you add custom entries to the container's hosts file, mapping hostnames to IP addresses like you'd do manually on your computer.
explanations.10: This line adds a hosts file entry so anything running in the container can access my_site.local and have it resolve to the IP 172.20.0.1, which is likely another container on the network.
explanations.14: external: true means this network already exists outside this Compose file—Docker won't try to create it, so you must have set it up beforehand.
